svg.title: The exact mean and variance require a noninteger trial count
svg.desc: Fixing exact mean five gives success probability five over n, so variance is five minus twenty-five over n for integer trial counts n at least five. Valid integer points near the candidate are plotted at n ten through fifteen. At n twelve, variance is thirty-five twelfths, below three. At n thirteen, variance is forty thirteenths, above three. The exact variance target three would require n twenty-five halves, shown as an orange cross between the valid integer counts. A real algebraic candidate of twelve and a half is not an admissible binomial trial count. This rejection uses exact moments, not rounded reports.
